Social Media Scams UK: Ads, Giveaways & DM Investments

Fake giveaways, paid ads for shops that do not exist, and investment pitches by DM. How to check an advertiser, a seller or a trader before you pay.

Social platforms compress the distance between a stranger and your money. An advert, a giveaway or a direct message can all reach you without you searching for anything, and each carries a different check.

The useful question is not whether an account looks real, but what happens if you are wrong. Paying a stranger by bank transfer removes the protection a card or a marketplace would have given you.

Adverts and shop fronts

A paid advert is not a recommendation, and a shop front inside an app is not a marketplace guarantee. Our Facebook ad scam guide covers checking an advertiser in Meta’s Ad Library — how long the page has run ads, and under what names. Our TikTok Shop scam guide covers sellers operating inside the app, where the protection that applies depends on how you paid rather than where you clicked.

Giveaways and prizes

A prize that needs a payment is not a prize. Our Instagram fake giveaway guide covers the copied-account version, where a real brand’s competition is mirrored by a near-identical handle that then asks for a delivery fee. Our X crypto giveaway guide covers the send-to-receive version, and why a checkmark no longer signals what it once did.

Investment pitches that arrive in a DM

Recruitment for investment fraud has largely moved into feeds and inboxes. Our Instagram investment scam guide covers profiles built around lifestyle proof, and our WhatsApp investment scam guide covers the private group or ‘mentor’ chat where screenshots of profits are shown to people who cannot verify them.

Before sending anything, check the firm on the FCA’s Financial Services Register, and check it is the firm you think it is rather than a clone using a real firm’s reference number.

Messages from people you do not know

An unexpected message from an unknown number is the opening move for several of these. Our WhatsApp stranger scam guide covers what the first few messages are testing for, and why replying at all has a cost.

Do not share a one-time code with anyone, whatever they say it is for. Codes sent to your phone are the last control standing between an attacker and your account.

How to pay, if you decide to

Paying by card gives you routes a bank transfer does not. A bank transfer to a stranger is closest to handing over cash, and marking a payment as ‘friends and family’ on a payment service removes the buyer protection that would otherwise apply.

If money has already gone, tell your bank it may be authorised push payment fraud; eligible claims are normally decided within five business days, with a maximum 35-business-day stop-clock.

How to report a social media scam in the UK

Report the account, advert or listing inside the platform, then report the fraud to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, or Police Scotland on 101 in Scotland.

Forward scam texts free to 7726 and suspicious emails to report@phishing.gov.uk.

Common questions

Does a verified checkmark mean an account is trustworthy?

No. On several platforms a checkmark can now be bought as part of a subscription, so it indicates a paid account rather than a confirmed identity. Check the account's history and its posting record instead.

A brand's giveaway asked me for a delivery fee. Is that normal?

It is a strong warning sign. Genuine prize draws do not ask winners for a payment to release a prize. Check the brand's own verified account and website rather than replying to the message.

How do I check an investment account I found on social media?

Look the firm up on the FCA's Financial Services Register yourself, and contact it using details from the Register rather than from the profile. Clone firms reuse a real firm's reference number, so matching a number alone is not enough.

Is a Facebook or Instagram advert checked before it runs?

Not in a way you can rely on. Meta's Ad Library lets you see what a page has advertised and for how long, which is a more useful signal than the advert itself.
